topic: For a name in Removing or RemovalReady
canonical_claim: For a name in `Removing` or `RemovalReady`, creation returns a typed retryable error stating that terminal fold, cleanup completion, and cursor retirement are pending; a DROP-driven targeted fold is not part of the correctness baseline.

topic: A scenario with needs_infra set is marked
canonical_claim: A scenario with `needs_infra` set is marked inconclusive and its `run` method is not executed when the two-replica plus RustFS compose cannot provide the required infrastructure.

topic: A lazy CAS table reattached as a
canonical_claim: A lazy CAS table reattached as a `StorageTableProxy` can block its first-access build in the ref-namespace LIST inside `CasRefLedger::ensureRefTableRecovered` for the entire object-store outage; the table self-heals after the store returns because the proxy job remains `OK` rather than entering a terminal `AsyncLoader` failure.

topic: CommandFsck::executeImpl does not throw for stale_edge in
canonical_claim: `CommandFsck::executeImpl` does not throw for `stale_edge` in either summary or detail mode, so a detail scan with nonzero `stale_edge` can print a `note:` and still exit with code 0.

topic: A referenced-but-missing or corrupt GC run, retired
canonical_claim: A referenced-but-missing or corrupt GC run, retired list, or adopted fold seal raises `CORRUPTED_DATA` and refuses the GC round until an operator performs GC rebuild.

topic: The arm-(a) decommission warning reports pool member
canonical_claim: The arm-(a) decommission warning reports pool member decommission underway: all N namespace(s) are still owned by this member; upcoming GC rounds perform the final cleanup — re-run this command afterwards to retire the slot, with a count from matching catalog entries; arm (b)'s stale-cut warning remains distinct.

topic: CommandFsck exposes a janitor-pending detail label and
canonical_claim: CommandFsck exposes a janitor-pending detail label and a non-throwing note with the pending count, bytes, and lives; it no longer claims that ca-decommission refuses these keys.

topic: clickhouse-disks cas-drop-member prints server_root_id= rather than srid=
canonical_claim: clickhouse-disks cas-drop-member prints server_root_id= rather than srid=, and its read-only error uses the same public name; no tree consumer parses the old srid= output key.

topic: ReadBufferFromS3::processException must check CurrentThread::get().isQueryCanceled() so a canceled
canonical_claim: `ReadBufferFromS3::processException` must check `CurrentThread::get().isQueryCanceled()` so a canceled query does not retry until `s3_max_single_read_retries` with backoff.

topic: MergeTreeDeduplicationLog must fail with an ordinary exception
canonical_claim: `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog` must fail with an ordinary exception when `current_writer` is null instead of relying on `chassert`.

topic: The CAS backup threat model defines five
canonical_claim: The CAS backup threat model defines five threats: T1 bucket/region loss, T2 operator error (`DROP TABLE`, bad mutation, wrong `rm`), T3 a CAS-layer bug (notably a GC bug deleting live data), T4 credential compromise, and T5 format dependence (whether restore requires a CAS-capable ClickHouse, any ClickHouse, or no ClickHouse at all).

topic: As an RTO optimization when a full
canonical_claim: As an RTO optimization when a full fetch is too slow, the storage policy can combine a fresh writable CA disk with the backup pool mounted as a readonly disk (claiming no lease or epoch, under the fsck/ca-gc-dryrun discipline): reads work within minutes straight off the backup, writes go to the fresh pool from minute one, and fetch degrades into a background hot-partitions-first drain by ordinary move machinery.

topic: RustFS stores each object as a directory
canonical_claim: RustFS stores each object as a directory containing an `xl.meta` file plus erasure part files (MinIO-style layout), which is the source of the roughly 2.2x on-disk store amplification observed relative to distinct payload size.

topic: A full CA-s3 lane post-mortem exonerated the
canonical_claim: A full CA-s3 lane post-mortem exonerated the B86 log-policy removal for the observed timeout growth: ProfileEvents on every stalled query showed zero CAS/RustFS wait, with threads parked on HTTP socket reads to public internet buckets (e.g. `clickhouse-datasets-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`) — the timeouts were external internet weather, not a CA regression. Additionally, The CA-s3 timeout investigation found stalled queries were bound to public web-disk HTTP reads, with zero CA/RustFS wait, so those timeouts were not caused by the CA changes.

topic: The DoS/amplification risk of SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED
canonical_claim: The DoS/amplification risk of `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` (SEC-6): rebuild does a full-universe discover-and-fold, O(all shards + all journals), so an attacker with SYSTEM privilege (or who can trigger repeated failures that tempt operators to rebuild) can make it an expensive, pool-wide, memory-heavy sweep sharing SEC-4's decode/fold exhaustion surface; recommended mitigation is rate-limiting/single-flight on the command plus streaming the fold.

topic: The reviewer verified that rebuild adds no
canonical_claim: The reviewer verified that rebuild adds no attack surface beyond SEC-3's total-compromise bar: an adversary who crafts an internally consistent owner state with refs silently removed could get rebuild to compute a baseline missing those edges, but the trimmed-history baseline guard detects truncated journals and fails closed, so producing an exploitable crafted state already requires full owner-plane write access (already total compromise). Residual open items: confirm the REBUILD RBAC grant is dedicated/narrow (not bundled into a broad SYSTEM grant), and confirm rebuild runs under GC leadership so it cannot race a live round into a split-baseline.

topic: In the CAS GC per-phase observability design
canonical_claim: In the CAS GC per-phase observability design, fsck_pre and fsck_post are each asserted clean individually but are never compared structurally against each other, despite an existing code comment promising such a comparison — a named, deliberately-unfixed gap rather than an oversight.

topic: Mode::EmulatedSingleProcess token bookkeeping is per-process and sharing
canonical_claim: `Mode::EmulatedSingleProcess` token bookkeeping is per-process and sharing such a pool between processes is not currently enforced against, so this mode can fail silently when misconfigured.

topic: The cache-over-CA startup diagnostic explicitly names the
canonical_claim: The cache-over-CA startup diagnostic explicitly names the `ca_cache` wrapper and recommends using the content-addressed disk directly in the storage policy until the combination is wired.

topic: A transient backend error on one disk
canonical_claim: A transient backend error on one disk is skipped by `system.cas_mounts` so it does not hide rows from other disks.

topic: No single backup tier covers the full
canonical_claim: No single backup tier covers the full threat matrix; the recommended composition is B1+B2 (in-pool `FREEZE`/retention-delayed-GC tier, near-free, a consistency anchor) plus the CAS-native backup pool (primary DR tier) plus native `BACKUP` at a rare weekly cadence (the only tier restorable without a CAS-capable binary), with logical export (Iceberg/Parquet) optionally as a fourth archival tier.

topic: In-place fail-over (mounting the backup bucket directly
canonical_claim: In-place fail-over (mounting the backup bucket directly as the new production pool) is documented as a last resort that consumes the backup at the first `PUT`; if ever used, `fsck` must run before the first write, GC and thinning must stay disabled until an operator explicitly enables them, and a new backup chain to a third bucket must start immediately.

topic: A 20,000-column wide part can issue about
canonical_claim: A 20,000-column wide part can issue about 20,000 object-store operations in one merge, exhausting the ClickHouse container's ephemeral TCP ports and causing `Poco::Net Cannot assign requested address` while the part itself can still commit correctly.

topic: A CA-s3 stateless-test baseline attribution ran the
canonical_claim: A CA-s3 stateless-test baseline attribution ran the 38 CA-s3-lane FAILs on the normal non-CA job: 31 also failed there (local-env noise, not CA-caused), leaving 7 CA-specific failures — 3 promote-vs-GC-condemn ABORTED, 2 timeouts, 1 TTL diff, 1 write-path memory issue — of which the 3 ABORTED were the meaningful production-robustness class.

topic: When gc/state is corrupted or missing a
canonical_claim: When `gc/state` is corrupted or missing a healthy adopted baseline, regular GC refuses every round, makes no further progress, and deletes nothing until `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` or `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild` is run.; The GC-rebuild validation plan (queued outside this plan) is: mid-soak `mc rm` of `gc/state` should make the guard's `CORRUPTED_DATA` appear in the GC round log with `outcome='Error'` and nothing deleted afterward, then `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` on one replica should let rounds resume and fsck converge to `dangling=0` with `pending-gc` draining.

topic: The GC crash-resume regime uses attempt-scoped write-once
canonical_claim: The GC crash-resume regime uses attempt-scoped write-once artifacts; an already-executed delete is replayed through the `NotFound` branch, and only the adopted attempt is reader-visible.

topic: A different-UUID stale mount remains a fail-closed
canonical_claim: A different-UUID stale mount remains a fail-closed `CORRUPTED_DATA` foreign-owner condition and requires operator guidance rather than automatic takeover.

topic: The GCS live validation fsck command is
canonical_claim: The GCS live validation fsck command is `clickhouse disks -C /etc/clickhouse-server/config.xml --disk ca_ro --query 'fsck'`, and the acceptance result is `dangling=0 unreachable=0 unaccounted=0`, `dedup_ratio=2`.

topic: The stand workaround for the ca_ro restart
canonical_claim: The stand workaround for the `ca_ro` restart issue is to remove `ca_ro` from server `config.d`, mount it through standalone `/etc/clickhouse-server/fsck-only.xml`, and invoke fsck with that configuration.

topic: The no-leftovers teardown sequence is deterministic GC
canonical_claim: The no-leftovers teardown sequence is deterministic GC drain, `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED UNMOUNT`, dormant `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FSCK`, then deletion of the pool directory.
